entry.title: I've Looked at Life From Both Sides Now
entry.summary:
by Tintinnabulation_of_the_Bells

One more game. You can do this, Adam, it’s just one more game.

It was one more game before their season ended and they had four months of time to do anything else besides crash in mediocre hotels and eat, sleep, and breathe hockey. One more night of heart-pounding, sweaty thrashing across the ice and throwing himself at his teammates and into the roar of whatever crowd they happened to attract that night and everything he lived for, everything he needed as much as the oxygen in his lungs.

Then four months of time off if he was lucky. The rest of his life if he was not.

 

An ECHL AU: Adam Birkholtz and Justin Oluransi don't meet until the ECHL, when Holster arrives straight from juniors and Ransom is seeking something, anything different after being forced to abandon his med school ambitions. For ten years, they're best friends and teammates and it's all they need. Except now Holster is a vet, his body could call it quits at a moment's notice, and he's not sure what waits for him on the other side of the abyss. If only he could ask Ransom to take the leap by his side.

The phone rings in Kent's ear. He waits. And waits. And—

“Kent.”

Her voice sounds different than Kent remembers it; not the fond, round edges or no-nonsense tones he was used to hearing, but blunt. Hollow. Even just on his name.

There’s static over the line, crackling over the thousands of miles and three time zones between them. Kent can still hardly believe that she, out of all the Zimmermanns, picked up.

“Mrs. Zimmermann,” he says after a moment too long being frozen, but now is thrown into action, his words scrambling over one another to get out of his mouth faster. “How is Jack? Please, is he okay? Nobody will tell me anything and he’s not picking up the phone, I even tried Bob but. Please. I just want to know he’s alright.”

entry.title: So The Universe Thinks Itself A Comedian
entry.summary:
by Bicyllium

Whimsy. That's what they call it, too. Whimsy.

Right.

--

Dex has been here for no more than a month. He's surrounded by his team, his weird as fuck team that talk loud in ways that his hometown never would have allowed. Bracketed by his linemate Nursey that he can't stand – for reasons he can't articulate nor tell anybody about – and the embodiment of some cosmic ideal of hope and light in Chowder.

He feels good. Feels accepted. Feels normal.

But he knows better to run his mouth. Knows not to let his words spill out without review, to taste what he's about to say and change its flavor accordingly, knows to always check with his Connoway gift how it could be received.

--

Magic is real, but is only ever inconvenient. Dex can taste intent, his worst of all. He hates his gift with all his heart. But worst of all, he hates lies. He hates Nursey for lying as much as he does, for his lies tasting as bad as his does. Maybe some day they stop lying altogether. Maybe some day when they are done being angry, they see each other for who they are.

Maybe that day is sooner than either of them think.
